judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 3 Skills in the Reading and Phonics Skill Area under the 'Phonic Activities three times a week for 15 minutes' (canonical Phonics) sub-strand: the first in Term 2 ('Uses words in written sentences that are pronounced the same way, but have different meanings... read/reed'), the second in Term 4 ('Spells words correctly using their phonic knowledge in informal tests, in dictation and in all written work'). They share genuine, pair-specific instructional coherence — both require applying phonic knowledge to produce correct words in written work — so they complement and reinforce each other. However, the Term 4 statement is not an expansion or deepening of the Term 2 homophone skill: the shared Learning Component 2e945841 records the same spelling statement also attached to a Grade 3 Term 2 SFI (eb60b722, path edf7e7dd/bf120d06/b99981ac/5b14664b) and another Grade 3 path, showing a statement repeated across terms at comparable demand rather than an increase in complexity that depends on homophone discrimination; the dependency direction is also unclear, since broad phonic spelling accuracy is at least as plausibly foundational as the homophone skill. The remaining nomination signals (shared Grade ancestor, rank gap 0, tokens 'and/in/words/written', tags 'phonics/written') are generic and cannot establish development. Canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the correct judgment; endpoint order is preserved and is not semantic. Evidence limits: source evidence truncated for both endpoints and LC evidence truncated for the second endpoint, and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so moderate confidence is retained.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Skills (rank 0) but sit in different strands: the first is Term 2 EMERGENT READING / Emergent reading skills ('Recognises own name and names of five other children in the class', LC tags: name recognition, print, sight words), while the second is Term 3 EMERGENT WRITING / Emergent Handwriting ('Copies patterns onto pegboards and words and letters onto paper', LCs: copying patterns onto pegboards; copying words and letters onto paper). They cohere substantively as complementary emergent-literacy work with printed words and letters — recognising name print and reproducing word/letter forms both develop print and letter awareness — but the evidence shows no dependency: the copying bullet is driven by fine-motor/handwriting development (pegboards, pattern copying), not by prior name recognition, and the only shared tokens are generic ('and', 'emergent', 'words'). Shared Grade R ancestor and weak rank proximity alone do not establish a developmental direction, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than a Term 2 to Term 3 buildsTowards.

Reliable correct spelling using phonic knowledge in dictation and written work therefore supports success with homophone discrimination and correct use. LC tags corroborate the shared phonics/spelling skill space (shared tags 'phonics', 'spelling'). judgment.rationale: Both resolved Skills sit in Grade 2, Term 4, WRITING, sub-strand 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' (same grade rank 2 and same term, so a within-term direction is permissible with substantive evidence). The first is a transcription/encoding skill ('Spells common words correctly and attempts to spell unfamiliar words using phonic knowledge', LCs: spelling of common words; phonic attempts at unfamiliar words); the second is extended composition ('Writes at least two paragraphs (ten sentences) on personal experiences or events'). Reliable spelling of common words plus phonic strategies for unfamiliar words materially supports the learner's ability to independently produce a ten-sentence, two-paragraph personal recount, whereas the composition task does not similarly underwrite spelling accuracy. The relation is supportive, not a mandated teaching sequence; shared ancestry, page 106 proximity and the single shared LC token 'writing' were not treated as sufficient on their own. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text and LCs.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Listening and Speaking (Oral) Skill bullets under the same 'Daily activities in all areas of Language and other subjects' sub-strand, with the first anchored in Term 3 ('Sings songs and rhymes and performs actions on own') and the second in Term 4 ('Recites poems and rhymes and adds actions to them with confidence'). Proficiency in independently singing rhymes with accompanying actions plausibly supports confident recitation of poems and rhymes with actions. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade R, Term 3, Emergent Reading, Sub-strand 'Phonological/Phonemic Awareness' skills printed in the same table row (rank 0, same term, so no grade/term ordering supports a developmental direction). The first is syllable-level work (clapping/drumbeating multisyllabic words into syllables and counting syllables); the second is rhyme identification in familiar rhymes, songs and rhyming sequences. These are distinct, parallel phonological-awareness sub-skills operating on different units of sound (syllables vs rimes); neither statement's text or Learning Components shows one extending, deepening, or presupposing the other, so proficiency in one is not evidenced as supporting success in the other. They are substantively coherent complementary components of the same oral phonological-awareness strand, supporting relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the bounded excerpts supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 2 Writing / Handwriting skills (same Grade rank 2), but the source evidence places the first in Term 1 (identity scope 'grade=grade 2|term=term 1|skill area=writing|sub strand=handwriting': 'Writes words with correct spacing between letters and words') and the second in Term 2 ('Uses appropriate spacing between words in a sentence.'). This is a permitted earlier-Term to later-Term direction within one grade. The change is substantive rather than mere repeated wording: Term 1 establishes spacing control at the letter-within-word and word level while copying/forming letters, whereas Term 2 applies spacing to words across a whole sentence in longer, more varied pieces of writing (per the Term 2 row context). Reliable spacing between letters and words plausibly supports success in maintaining appropriate word spacing across a sentence, so first_to_second buildsTowards is supported. Endpoint source evidence is truncated and both endpoints and their ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, but the retained statement text, Term scope and Handwriting sub-strand placement are unambiguous for this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills are Grade 2 (rank 2), Term 4, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics', printed in adjacent rows of the same Grade 2 Term 4 table (window 38): 'Reads aloud to a partner' (Paired/Independent Reading sub-strand, row 5) and 'Reads words from phonics lessons in sentences and other texts' (Phonics / 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes' sub-strand, row 4). They form substantive, pair-specific instructional coherence: applying taught phonic words within sentences and connected texts is the word-recognition counterpart to orally reading continuous text with a peer, and the two are complementary components of the same term's reading programme. This coherence goes beyond the single shared token 'reads', the shared Skill Area/Term/Grade ancestors, and weak page proximity. However, the statements are concurrent within one Grade and one Term, in different sub-strands, with no evidence of extension, deepening, increased independence, longer or harder text, or any other capability growth from one to the other; a directional buildsTowards would rest on a general decoding-to-fluency pedagogical claim rather than on this pair's curriculum evidence, so the symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Material limitations: both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context, both have truncated source and supporting LC evidence (24 omitted source evidence items each), and the shared Grade 2 and Term 4 ancestors are merged banner nodes, so hierarchy signals are weak support only; confidence is moderate accordingly.
